description: STRONG ADMISSION, the two title arms that measure as high-precision on their own: `replicat* and/& extend*` and the qualifier family (`direct|conceptual|registered|exact|close|high-powered|pre-registered|large-scale|many-labs|multi-site replication(s)`). Both are carried VERBATIM from the twelve-arm `replication-claim-title` this splits — no regex was retuned in the split, so a row's membership is unchanged and only the attribution and the shadow flag move. WHY THE SPLIT. Per-arm labels showed the twelve arms are not one population. Arm 3 reads 99.2% apparent precision on 131 labels and arm 6 reads 86.5% on 96; together they admit 4,237 of the 10,304 rows at 94.1% (95% Wilson 90.3–96.4%, n=237: 223 yes, 9 no, 5 unclear) and hold 205 known-FLoRA papers. The other ten arms carry the false-positive load — arm 12's negation matrix reads 20.0%, arm 9's success framing 25.0%, arm 11's failure nouns 50.0% — and now live in `replication-claim-title-broad`, so each half can be promoted, priced and retired on its own evidence. This tier is the one sized to be affordable: roughly $7 at the screen's measured $161/100k, against $17 for all twelve arms. WHAT WAS REJECTED. A 22-clause meta-discussion exclusion list fitted to this pair's own nine labelled false positives reported 97.4%, and that number is not usable: it was developed and evaluated on the same nine errors, and checking it row by row showed it removed 8 errors AND one genuine replication. An exclusion list that already destroys a true positive in the sample it was fitted to will destroy more outside it. This is the same lesson the single rule recorded — whole-tier exclusions moved precision from 80.7% to 81.9% (biological) and 83.4% (biological+meta), while the positive citation requirement reached 97.2% — and the split honours it by narrowing through ARM SELECTION, a pre-specified positive requirement, rather than through a list of senses to exclude. Composites adding a bare year or `et al` to these two arms were measured too and land at 94.3–94.6% with confidence intervals fully overlapping this one: nothing beat the simple pair, so the simple pair ships. PRECEDENCE 750, inherited from the rule this splits, so nothing else in the book reorders. It yields to `replication-claim-cited-title` (760), which is this claim with a named target, and to the identifier/title/type discards (940–960) that say the record is not a paper at all; it outranks `replication-claim-title-broad` (740), `replication-claim-text` (730) and `not-a-study-type` (500), whose claim is a fallible registry crosswalk — so a replication mistyped as `paratext` is screened rather than deleted. Every tier of this family routes to the same pile, so precedence decides ATTRIBUTION, not destination: which tier `filter_evidence` records for a row several tiers claim. `vocabulary` stays null across the family: admission to the two-voter screen is a request for attention, not a verdict about what the row is (CONVENTIONS.md, "Pile → paper_type"). OPEN: the 205-paper FLoRA capture is a third of the ~578 the full title tier holds. That is the deliberate cost of the narrowing and the reason the broad tier is a separate promotable spec rather than deleted arms — recall is what we care about, precision is only what we can measure.

measured.rationale: Promoted to production by maintainer decision, 2026-08-05: the two arms carried verbatim from the twelve-arm family are the high-precision pair, and the split existed precisely so they could be promoted without buying the broad ten. The broad twin stays in shadow.

measured.sample: Volumes counted exactly over routing release 93b6d1acbc3c (the current release, 5,146,160-row pool) by applying each arm to the titles of the 10,304 rows this family would newly admit — rows not already screened by replication-claim-cited-title, not lost to a higher-precedence discard, and not no_text. NOT a scaled estimate: `analysis/` scratch reproduces it by joining routing+evaluations to the pool parquet. Precision from the same blind Claude Sonnet label pass of 2026-08-04 used by the single rule this splits: 584 title-position rows drawn stratified by arm, titles only, field-neutral rubric. Precision here is APPARENT precision — a model's titles-only judgement, an upper bound on what the two-voter screen would confirm — and is reported raw with unclear counted as a miss, with a 95% Wilson interval. Post-stratifying to the pool's primary-arm mix moves it to 94.2%, i.e. not at all: the stratified sample is near-proportional for these two arms (pool 57.8/42.2, sample 57.7/42.3).
measured.rationale: 4,237 of the 10,304 newly-admissible rows, 205 known-FLoRA papers, 94.1% apparent precision (95% Wilson 90.3–96.4%; 223 yes / 9 no / 5 unclear of 237 labelled rows falling in the selection). Per-arm: arm 3 (`replicat* and/& extend*`) 99.2% on n=131, arm 6 (qualifier family) 86.5% on n=96. Counting unclear as a miss is the conservative reading; excluding it gives 96.1%. This rule admits and does not discard, so the evidence gate does not bind it (CONVENTIONS.md: "A rule that cannot admit needs no evidence at all") — this entry documents the claim that justified splitting the arms, not a gate.
